items.claim: The closing WEB excerpt at Jer.50.13 is not byte-verbatim and lacks its own inline citation, and the boundary prose misattributes its parallel formula to the current chapter rather than to Jer.49, where it actually sits.
items.evidence: The staged WEB text at Jer.50.13 opens “Everyone who goes by Babylon will be astonished, and hiss at all her plagues.” (capital E); the row's own prose instead renders it 'everyone who goes by Babylon will be astonished, and hiss at all her plagues' (lowercase, no inline web: citation paired with it, only the oshb: citation for the accompanying Hebrew splice). The four ketiv/qere pairs spliced at Jer.50.11 are all byte-accurate against the source and the count matches the inventory, so the seam's own textual grounding is not in question.

items.claim: The opening WEB excerpt splices two non-adjacent parts of the verse with an ellipsis and presents them inside one curly quotation as if continuous, omitting an emphatic clause that the row's own paired Hebrew splice shows is actually present.
items.evidence: The staged WEB text at Jer.50.21 reads “Go up against the land of Merathaim, even against it, and against the inhabitants of Pekod.”; the row's own curly-quoted excerpt instead reads 'Go up against the land of Merathaim...and against the inhabitants of Pekod,' silently dropping “even against it,” with an ellipsis rather than quoting a contiguous span. The row's own paired Hebrew splice for this same excerpt is byte-complete and includes the words corresponding to the dropped clause, so the omission is not a byte-accuracy problem in the Hebrew but a verbatim violation in how the English is presented as one continuous quotation. The two further excerpts in the same field (“Kill and utterly destroy after them” and “and do according to all that I have commanded you”) are both byte-verbatim. The setumah closing the row at Jer.50.21 is correctly disclosed and the one-verse span itself is not in question.
